summary: Round 11, narrow re-check against the round-10 bytes (75bf7082). Still prose only: no production logic, no wire change, and nothing in this diff adds, moves or authorises an object-store request. I checked only the two cells named as changed and did not re-derive a decision or a counted fact. WHAT HOLDS. My round-10 major is discharged on its HARD half: the obligation now lives in M5.45h's own criterion 1 at backlog.md:69, which is todo today and in the file this diff already edits, with the reason recorded in place (M5.66 may make the operation a header range plus one union slice -- two requests, O(1) in K) and with M5.66's cell at backlog.md:126 no longer claiming it can write that distinction later ('THE DISTINCTION IS WRITTEN INTO M5.45h's OWN CRITERION 1 BY THE COMMIT THAT CREATES THIS ROW'). The unactionable window -- M5.66 owing a criteria edit to a row it depends on -- is gone from both sites. And everything I passed at rounds 7-9 in M5.66's cell survives the criterion-2 restatement byte-for-byte in substance: the two-sided boundary pair (exactly two requests and fewer bytes at K = crossover; exactly one request and exactly the whole-object bytes at crossover + 1), the symmetric round-trip predicate, the codec read-and-refuse arm with the GoldenSegmentV1Test fixture route, 3b's extent disagreement, the ~400 whole-object mandate, the count-every-request-at-the-seam clause, and the M5.45g + M5.45h dependency with its verified ground. The new invariants (i) and (iii) are strictly stronger than the sampled shares they replace, and the sampled cases are correctly demoted to minimum evidence with K = 2 added at the hostile small-K end. TWO THINGS BLOCK, BOTH INSIDE THE TWO CELLS I WAS ASKED TO CHECK, AND BOTH ARE THE SAME SHAPE: a correction applied to one of two places. (A) I CANNOT CONFIRM THE READING I WAS ASKED TO CONFIRM. Constant-in-K preserves the literal 1's mutations only if the count is sampled at more than one K, and M5.45h names exactly one share -- K = 64, four times, and no other. 'A per-run implementation reports 64 at K = 64, not a constant' is an inference the case cannot make from one observation: 64 is indistinguishable from a constant 64 without a second K. The soft half of my round-10 repair therefore did not land, and M5.66's own cell shows the standard it was held to -- it restated criterion 2 as invariants over all K precisely because sampled shares do not pin a shape, and then kept five samples as evidence for them. M5.45h states a property over all K and keeps one. (B) The span/sum correction half-landed: criterion 2 now carries BOTH bounds, (ii) span and, later in the same criterion, the unretracted sum sentence the cell itself says is the earlier wording. On this cell's own arithmetic they differ by 7,403,852 bytes at K = 169. Detail below. Both repairs are one clause each, in the file this diff already stages.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:69 (M5.45h criterion 1: 'asserted at K = 64' together with 'THE COUNT IS ASSERTED CONSTANT IN K RATHER THAN AS THE LITERAL 1' and 'CONSTANT-IN-K KILLS EVERY MUTATION THE LITERAL 1 KILLED: a per-run implementation reports 64 or 128 at K = 64, not a constant')
findings.title: Constancy is unfalsifiable at one sample: K = 64 is the ONLY share M5.45h names, so 'constant in K' pins no number where the literal 1 pinned one -- and the owner's only writable assertion is a literal, which puts M5.66's owner back in front of the landed-assertion weakening this clause was added to prevent
findings.failure_scenario:
THE ARITHMETIC OF THE SUBSTITUTION. Under the literal 1 the expected value is pinned: a per-run implementation reports 64 at K = 64, 64 != 1, red, from a one-line assertion. Under 'constant in K' the expected value is unpinned, and constancy is a property of a FUNCTION of K -- it is not decidable from a single evaluation of it. I grepped the cell: 'K = 64' occurs four times and no other K appears anywhere in M5.45h. So the case the criterion authorises observes exactly one value, and 64 at K = 64 is indistinguishable from a constant 64. The cell's own justification sentence makes the inference the case cannot make.

WALK THE OWNER. M5.45g and M5.62 land, M5.45h is taken. The owner needs an assertion form for 'the count is constant in K' and has one share. There is nothing to compare against, so they must write a literal. Two branches, both bad. (i) They write isEqualTo(1) -- correct today, and the clause has bought NOTHING: M5.66's owner switches on the bounded path, the count at K = 64 becomes 2, and they face exactly the two exits this clause exists to close, weaken a landed assertion in another row's test (non-negotiable 2, testing.md rule 5, invisible to check-test-integrity across rows) or abandon the bounded path at K = 64. That is my round-10 major returning with the words changed. (ii) They take the clause at face value, decline to pin 1 because the clause tells them not to, and write the weakest thing one sample supports -- isEqualTo(fetchCount at the only K run), isLessThan(K), or isPositive(). Then the per-run implementation the whole row exists to kill goes green: 64 fetch invocations at K = 64, which at production's ~400-of-1,600 node share is ~400 whole-object GETs against one 8 MiB object, the shards-per-node scaling this cell's own preamble names as forbidden by non-negotiable 6. Neither branch is contrived; the criterion offers no third.

AND THE CELL IS INTERNALLY AT ODDS ON THE SAME POINT: the headline of criterion 1 still reads 'a node holding K runs of one segment issues ONE fetch', which pins 1, while the later clause says explicitly not the literal 1. An owner reading top to bottom gets both.

THE STANDARD IS SET IN THE OTHER CELL THIS DIFF EDITS. M5.66's criterion 2 was restated this very round as 'AN INVARIANT OVER ALL K, NOT A LIST OF SAMPLED SHARES, AND THAT IS THE LESSON OF NINE BREAKS' and then keeps FIVE samples (K = 2, 64, crossover, crossover + 1, ~400) as minimum evidence for it. M5.45h now states a property over all K and keeps one sample. The lesson was applied to one of the two cells the same commit edits.

WHAT CLOSES IT, one clause and one extra case: assert the count at TWO shares and require them EQUAL -- K = 2 and K = 64, matching M5.66's own low case. Per-run gives 2 against 64 and reds. One-operation-per-(node, segment) gives 1 and 1 and greens. M5.66's header-plus-slice gives 2 and 2 and greens with no edit to a landed assertion, which is the whole point of the axis. The decode half is unaffected: all K runs still decode their own records at each share, so the empty-array coalescer still reds. Equally admissible and no weaker: 'the count is at most 2 at every K, asserted at K = 2 and K = 64', which is falsifiable per-sample AND independent of K.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2: invariant '(ii) the bytes it fetches are at most the header range plus the SPAN of the K extents -- max(byteStart + byteLen) - min(byteStart) -- plus a stated constant' against the surviving later sentence 'AND BYTES ARE BOUNDED ABOVE, NOT ONLY "STRICTLY FEWER": at most the header range plus the sum of byteLen plus a stated constant')
findings.title: The span-for-sum correction half-landed: criterion 2 now carries BOTH byte bounds as live obligations, differing by 7,403,852 bytes at K = 169 on this cell's own figures, and the cell's own note says the sum wording is the earlier one while the earlier one is still physically in the criterion
findings.failure_scenario:
BOTH SENTENCES ARE IMPERATIVE AND NEITHER IS MARKED SUPERSEDED. The new invariant (ii) bounds on the SPAN. Roughly 2,000 characters later the same criterion still says, in bold, 'AND BYTES ARE BOUNDED ABOVE, NOT ONLY "STRICTLY FEWER": at most the header range plus the sum of byteLen plus a stated constant'. The only acknowledgement is inside the (ii) clause -- 'an earlier wording said sum while the same sentence mandated fetching the span' -- which is a claim about a wording that has been REMOVED. It has not been. An owner enumerating criterion 2's obligations top to bottom collects two mutually exclusive bounds on the same quantity.

THE GAP IS NOT A ROUNDING DIFFERENCE, and the cell supplies both numbers: at K = 169 the union span is 8,289,919 bytes against a sum of 169 * 5,243 = 886,067 -- a factor of 9.4, 7,403,852 bytes apart. The mandated implementation IS the span: 'the header range and ONE UNION SLICE'. So the owner has three outcomes, and the criterion selects none. (i) Obey the surviving sum sentence with a KiB-scale constant, as 'a stated constant' next to a 78,400-byte header range reads: criterion 2 reds the union slice at K = crossover, the very case it mandates, and the compliant shapes left are the removal arm chosen on a wording artifact or one ranged GET per run -- which fetches exactly sum(byteLen), is the ONLY shape a tight sum bound admits, and is 170 requests against 1 at K = 169, the runs-per-node scaling non-negotiable 6 forbids by name. This cell states the rule against itself: 'A criterion that reds the intended implementation is worse than a loose one, because it looks strict.' (ii) Obey (ii) and leave the sum sentence plainly violated at every K the row asserts, so the row lands with a stated criterion unmet and a reviewer at M5.66 reading a red criterion as satisfied because a later paragraph says otherwise. (iii) Set the sum constant to ~7.8 MB to admit the union, which is the horn (ii) was written to escape -- 93% of the object, 2.1% tighter than the 'strictly fewer' it exists to strengthen, and it lets the open-ended bytes=byteStart- survivor back in.

THE ROW NAMES THIS DEFECT AS ITS OWN: 'a correction applied to one of two places is this milestone's most repeated defect' and 'the half-landed fix this task has now produced six times'. This is that shape, inside the criterion the same edit rewrote.

WHAT CLOSES IT: delete the clause 'at most the header range plus the sum of byteLen plus a stated constant' from the later sentence and leave it carrying only what is still true and still needed there -- the open-ended bytes=byteStart- survivor it names (which (ii) already kills: at K = 2 the span is ~2.80 MB and the suffix ~5.59 MB) and the ~400 whole-object mandate, which is independent of the bound. One deletion, no new obligation, and the arithmetic in (ii)'s own note becomes true of the cell as written.
